claims.text: FeCoCrNiAl0.5 can possess a dual-phase FCC/BCC microstructure.
The proposed starting coating has a nanocrystalline grain structure and well-defined FCC/BCC interfaces.
The proposed starting coating has low initial dislocation and twin densities.
Deformation twinning occurs in the FCC phase of dual-phase FeCoCrNiAl0.5.
FCC/BCC interphase boundaries act as nanoscale barriers to dislocation motion.
Deformation twins in the FCC phase create additional obstacles to dislocation climb.
Deformation twins in the FCC phase impede lattice diffusion.
The combined interphase-boundary and twinning mechanisms delay the evolution of steady-state creep deformation.
Fine-grained CoCrFeNiMn has been subjected to constant-stress tensile creep tests at 500–600 °C with microstructural examination during steady-state creep.
At 500–600 °C under sustained stress, the proposed dual-phase coating will activate both dislocation-mediated plasticity and lattice diffusion.
A dual-phase alloy with active FCC twinning will have a lower steady-state creep strain rate than a similar baseline with reduced twinning or fewer interphase boundaries.
A dual-phase alloy with active FCC twinning will exhibit greater work hardening during continuous loading than the proposed baseline.
The interphase-boundary and twinning mechanism will dominate when temperature and stress are sufficient to activate conventional dislocation creep and lattice diffusion.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at very low temperature or stress when dislocation creep and lattice diffusion are inactive.
Prior evidence supports individual contributions from interphase-boundary pinning and deformation twinning to creep resistance.
Oxidation and grain growth could affect the measured creep response.
Suppressing twinning while maintaining similar phase fractions provides a controlled comparison of the proposed mechanism.
Similar steady-state creep rates and work-hardening behavior in the twin-suppressed and conventional coatings would falsify the proposed dominance of the combined mechanism.
